title: OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI
summary: Makes a prim the root of a volume or surface deformable body. Enumerated by usd-schemas CONTAINS OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI. The prim must be a Mesh, TetMesh or BasisCurves, or an Xformable that is not a Gprim, and its point-based subtree must hold exactly one simulation mesh (OmniPhysicsVolumeDeformableSimAPI or OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableSimAPI) on the prim itself or an immediate child, plus an enabled PhysicsCollisionAPI mesh; otherwise no body is created.

columns.name: omniphysics:deformableBodyEnabled
columns.absent: false (the parser's default), not USD's true: the body gets a runtime record but no PhysX deformable, and its PhysicsCollisionAPI meshes are no longer excluded from the rigid collider scan. Write true.
columns.notes: A change releases and re-parses the body; the column has no in-place update.

columns.name: omniphysics:mass
columns.absent: 0.0: no explicit mass; see the sentinel rule.
columns.sentinel: Any value <= 0 (the schema fallback 0 included) means no explicit mass: the walker stores -1 and the per-vertex masses come from the bound deformable material's omniphysics:density, or, when that is <= 0 or there is no material, from a default density of 1000 kg/m^3 (volume) or 100 kg/m^3 (surface) converted to stage units.
columns.notes: Re-read on change; the deformable body update stores the new value and recomputes the per-vertex masses.

interactions.rule: kinematicEnabled, startsAsleep and simulationOwner are read on this prim only when OmniPhysicsBodyAPI is listed in usd-schemas as well.

The single simulation mesh in the subtree decides the body kind: volume for OmniPhysicsVolumeDeformableSimAPI, surface for OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableSimAPI. A second simulation mesh, or one below an immediate child, drops the body silently.

The first point-based prim in the subtree with PhysicsCollisionAPI (physics:collisionEnabled not false) is the collision mesh. None logs 'No UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI found on deformable body prim or sub-tree' and no body is created; a volume body needs a tet collision mesh, a surface body its simulation mesh as collision mesh.

The material bound to the simulation mesh supplies the PhysX deformable material and the density for the mass when it was created as the matching kind: a volume material (OmniPhysicsDeformableMaterialAPI without the surface API) for a volume body, a surface material (OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI) for a surface body. Otherwise the scene's default deformable material of that kind is used.
The walker looks for a bindPose instance on the simulation, collision, skin and cooking-source meshes of the subtree.

notes: The runtime also reads physics:filteredPairs and the PhysxBaseDeformableBodyAPI, PhysxSurfaceDeformableBodyAPI and PhysxAutoDeformableBodyAPI columns on this prim; those belong to their own components.
Body creation also requires a scene with the full GPU pipeline; otherwise it logs an error and creates no body.
